headline: Shu, “owner”, is from Middle Chinese 主 (MC tsyuX), in the kan'on pronunciation.
Unnun is from Middle Chinese 云云 (MC hjun hjun), with un becoming nun by renjō, and is first cited to 1110.
サボる is a clipping of サボタージュ (sabotāju, “idling, truancy”) plus る (-ru, verb-forming suffix), the former from French sabotage.
Nazukeru is 名 (na) plus 付ける (tsukeru), with tsukeru voiced to zukeru by rendaku.
Gekirei is from the Middle Chinese compound 激勵 (MC kek ljejH).
Ōi is an elongation of おい.
Tōtobu is 尊 (tōto, the stem of 尊い (tōtoi, “noble, exalted, sacred”)) plus ぶ (-bu, “to act like”).
Kuki is from Old Japanese, attested in the Kakyō Hyōshiki of 772 with the phonetic spelling 倶基.
Asa is from Old Japanese and is likely cognate with a Korean word for hemp.
Naizō is 内 (“inside”) plus 蔵 (“to store”).
Sokkenai is a shift from 素気ない (sugenai).
Kaerimiru is 帰り (kaeri, the stem of 帰る (kaeru, “to return, to go home”)) plus 見る (miru, “to look, to watch, to take care”).
Issai is from the Middle Chinese compound 一切, in the goon reading, which is probably the earlier import.
スペース is from English space.
ファイト is from English fight.
Mapputatsu is 真っ (ma'-, “truly”) plus 二つ (futatsu, “two parts”).
Yami is from Old Japanese, with ultimate roots uncertain, and may be cognate with 病む (yamu, “to be ill”) and 止む (yamu, “to stop, to quit”).
セット is borrowed from English set.
データ is borrowed from English data.
Suru, “to rub”, is from Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *suru.
Sententeki is 先天 (senten, “congenital”) plus 的 (-teki, “-like”).
Teibō is from the Middle Chinese compound 堤防, literally “dike, embankment + dike”.
Minamoto is derived from 水 (mi, “water”), な (na, Old Japanese possessive particle) and 元 (moto, “origin, source”).
Tomonau is from classical 伴ふ (tomonafu), formed from とも (tomo, “companion”) plus なふ (nafu, verb-forming suffix).
Eiji is 英 (ei, “English”) plus 字 (ji, “character, letter”).
Toho is a Sino-Japanese word from 徒步, maybe from Middle Chinese.
Kikon is 既 (ki, “already”) plus 婚 (kon, “marriage”).
Sōdai is from Middle Chinese 壮大 (MC dajH|daH).
Orimono is 織り (ori, the stem of 織る (oru), weaving, woven) plus 物 (mono, “thing”).
ビジネス is from English business.
Kottōhin is, by surface analysis, 骨董 (kottō) plus 品 (-hin).
